source_title: Patrick Stewart passes away: Hollywood celebs pay tribute
source_excerpt: Hollywood is mourning the loss of one of its most beloved screen legends - Sir Patrick Stewart.The actor, who captivated generations of viewers as the cerebral Captain Jean-Luc Picard in 'Star Trek: The Next Generation' and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the 'X-Men' franchise, passed away on Wednesday. He was 86. The actor reportedly died at his Los Angeles home, following what his spokesperson described as a âbrief and poignant journeyâ with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to a statement shared on his X account.Soon after the news broke, tributes poured in from across the entertainment industry, with Hugh Jackman, William Shatner, the Russo Brothers and Marvel Studios among those honouring the veteran actor. Co-stars, colleagues and fans remembered Stewart's extraordinary legacy, celebrating a career that spanned decades and left an indelible mark on both television and cinema.Patrick Stewart's Marvel family mourns his demiseHugh Jackman, who co-starred with Patrick Stewart in 8 films over the years, primarily through the X-Men franchise and a 2026 comedy, paid poignant tribute to his late friend. Sharing photos from behind the scenes on the big stage and their time on the sets of 'Logan', he wrote, "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."Marvel Studios released a statement honouring his legacy that began with his stint in 'X-Men' and will reportedly conclude with his final turn in 'Avengers: Doomsday'. The statement read, âAll of us at Marvel Studios are deeply saddened by the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart. Sir Patrick brought Professor Charles Xavier to life with extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from X-Men to Logan to Avengers: Doomsday. He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art.âRebecca Romijn, who starred with Patrick in both X-Men and Star Trek, shared a video message that she captioned "What a gift to have been your friend. Rest in peace, dear Patrick."'Avengers: Doomsday' director-duo the Russo Brothers also took to their handles to pay tribute. Sharing a still of Stewart from what is said to be his final film, they wrote, "Weâve been lucky enough to work with some of our childhood heroes. And Sir Patrick Stewart will always be one of them. A legendary actor with an unmistakeable presence, and an unmatched integrity. Thank you for entertaining all of us, sir. And for teaching us humanity, both on and off the screen. Sending our love to your family, friends, and fans around the world."Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige also paid tribute to Stewart in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter, he said, "Away from the cameras, he was even more remarkable, with a wonderfully sharp sense of humor. It was a true privilege to know him and to work with him. His legacy lives on not only in decades of extraordinary work, but in the many, many people he mentored. He will be deeply missed.âDafne Keen who starred in 'Logan', also paid tribute to Patrick Stewart in a note that read, âI heard of Patrickâs passing earlier today, which is funny in a kismet kind of way, considering I was drafting an email to send him late last night, something I hadnât done in quite some time.He was such a kind, genuine, funny, unique, caring and charming man. I remember his endless jokes, nurturing nature and colourful reading glasses. Every single day spent working by his side was an honour and a privilege I can't quite believe I had. He was a walking master of his craft, and of life. One of the greatest of our time, on stage and on screen.I have always looked up to him, and always will. As an actor and as a man. He had a wonderful way of wrapping every ancient lesson he imparted in wonder, fun and excitement. I will always remember his warmth and the respect he showed to everyone around him.I will forever hold those months we spent together close to my heart, and will always think of him as a pivotal part of how I view the world around me.So rest in peace, you giant, you legend amongst men. The beautiful work, humanity and kindness you leave behind will live on forever.âThe Academy honours Patrick StewartIn a heartfelt tweet, the Academy wrote, "There was something extraordinary about the way Sir Patrick Stewart could make even the most powerful characters feel profoundly human.Whether commanding the bridge of the Enterprise or guiding a generation of young mutants, Sir Patrick Stewart brought a tenderness to his characters that made us feel we knew them. Behind that unmistakable voice was an actor who understood that even the greatest heroes could be uncertain, that strength could exist alongside vulnerability, and that compassion was never a weakness.Over a career spanning more than six decades, his performances became woven into the lives of generations who grew up watching him. As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Professor Charles Xavier, and so many others, he left us with characters we loved, lessons we carried, and memories we'll always treasure."The SAG-AFTRA also paid tribute in a post that read, "Sir Patrick Stewart will live on in our hearts and memories through his remarkable career spanning the British stage, television and film. Our condolences to his family, friends, colleagues and a galaxy of fans. #SagAftraMember since 1987."MacFarlane, who worked with Stewart on numerous projects, including Family Guy, Ted, Blunt Talk and American Dad!, penned a heartfelt note that read, "Patrick was one of those icons who we somehow all took for granted would always be with us.I grew up as a fan, and was later gifted the privilege of becoming a colleague and friend, working with him for many years on âAmerican Dad!â, âFamily Guyâ, and âTedâ. He was that rare actor who could take any bit of dialogue and elevate it, making a good writer sound great, and a great writer sound masterful. He was also as humble as they come. I remember exchanging emails with him a number of years ago when he was beginning day 1 of a new film. He commented to me that he always walked onto a new set feeling like the biggest novice there. My stunned reaction was the same as anyoneâs would be. I said, âPatrick, if you feel that way, the rest of us are screwed.â We have lost a legendary actor today, and for many of us, a good friend. He will be deeply missed by the entire planet."Star Trek family remembers Patrick StewartStewart's former co-star William Shatner, who played Captain James T. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. Rest in the heavens, Captain.âCelebs mourn Patrick Stewart's demiseTributes poured in on social media from all sections, including celebs, friends, former costars and even organisations that the late actor supported.Dave Blass wrote, âThis was the moment I had dream of, the moment I had feared. Patrick Stewart walking onto the bridge of the USS Enterprise that I had recreated. Would he hate it would he love it. What would this moment feel like.
